name: Verb Base Form
summary: The base form is the simple form of a verb, with no endings. It is used with I, you, we, they, and after do/does in negatives and questions.
explanation: Every English verb has five forms: base, third-person singular (-s), past, past participle, and present participle (-ing). The base form is the dictionary form. It is used after I/you/we/they, after modal verbs (can, will, should), and in negative and question sentences with do/does/did.

form_notes.base_with_i_you_we_they: With I, you, we, they, use the base form of the verb.
form_notes.base_after_does_not: With he/she/it in negatives, after does not, the verb returns to the base form.
form_notes.base_after_do_question: In questions with Do/Does, the verb appears in the base form.

common_error_explanations.err_01: With I/you/we/they, the verb takes the base form without -s.
common_error_explanations.err_02: After does in questions, the main verb returns to the base form (no -s).
